name: On/Off DIN Rail Module
description: A relay module that mounts on a DIN rail in an electrical panel to switch lighting circuits on and off remotely over Insteon.

steps.text: Turn off the breaker or fuse and verify that the power is off.
Disconnect the wires from the light fixture and strip 5/16 in. (8 mm) of bare wire on the ends.
Making sure the wires are not touching, turn on the breaker or fuse.
Use a voltage meter to identify the fixture's line, load and neutral wires.
Turn off the breaker or fuse again.
Write down the Insteon ID on the side of the module and the load it controls.
Snap the module onto the DIN rail, leaving 3/4 in. (2 cm) between modules for heat dissipation.
Connect the line, neutral, load and sense wires per the diagram for your installation.
Make sure the wires are firmly connected and no bare wire is exposed.
Turn on the breaker or fuse.
steps.expect: After a few seconds the load turns on and the LED turns green

steps.text: Test by tapping the paddle top and bottom.
steps.expect: Load turns on and off; LED is green when the load is on and red when it is off

steps.text: If wired to a single or dual momentary switch, set the switch operation mode: press and hold the SET button until it beeps three times.
steps.expect: Three beeps; LED blinking green, red, then green

steps.text: Slowly tap the SET button four times for single momentary or five times for dual momentary.
Press and hold the SET button until it double-beeps.
steps.expect: LED stops blinking and shows green if the load is on or red if it is off

notes: The module defaults to latching switch mode.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds, until the module beeps.

notes: To link, press and hold the controller's button until it beeps, set the responder to the desired state, then press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps; the controller double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.
As a responder, the module answers by pressing and holding its SET button until it double-beeps while the controller is in linking mode.
The 3-second hold time and the four-minute timeout come from the Global Line Developer Notes; software can send the Enter Linking Mode command for the same result.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds, until the module beeps.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder, and the device's group 1 to the Hub as a controller, so the Hub receives the device's reports.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request, Enter Linking Mode and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.
Tap the SET button.
For each responder, adjust it to the desired scene state.
Press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps.
Press and hold the SET button until the module double-beeps.
Test by tapping the module on and off.
steps.expect: All the responders turn on and off

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.
Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps a second time.
steps.expect: LED blinks red; the module is in unlinking mode

notes: To remove a link, put the controller in unlinking mode first, then press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps.

To unlink several responders in one session, tap the SET button after entering unlinking mode (LED double-blinks red), press and hold each responder's SET button until it double-beeps, then press and hold the module's SET button until it double-beeps to finish.

steps.text: Remove the module from every controller's scenes (see unlinking), otherwise controllers keep retrying commands and create network delays.
Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.
Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps a second time.
Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps a third time.
Slowly tap the SET button three times.
Press and hold the SET button and do not let go.
Release the SET button after the beeping stops.
steps.expect: After a few seconds the module double-beeps, turns on and the LED turns green

steps.text: For each responder the module controls, put the module in unlinking mode.
Press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps.
For each controller that controls the module, put the controller in unlinking mode.
Press and hold the module's SET button until it double-beeps.

notes: The On/Off DIN Rail Module 2453 Owner's Manual says to remove all of the module's responder links before uninstalling it; otherwise controllers keep retrying commands and create network delays.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Enter Unlinking Mode, Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

sources: On/Off DIN Rail Module 2453 Owner's Manual
On/Off DIN Rail Module 2453 Quick Start Guide
